newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia media laws won't favour anyone - PM.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia media laws won't favour anyone - PM.

text.p: Australian Prime Minister John Howard said on Monday the government wanted to ensure that any changes to media ownership laws would not be aimed at any one media proprietor.
"No matter what you do in media policy, somebody there will say that you are favouring one or another of the media proprietors," Howard told Australian Broadcasting Corp radio.
"We're going to try very hard to make our reforms non-mogul specific," he said.
The government is currently reviewing cross-media ownership laws, which it has described as antiquated and inflexible.
Howard declined to comment on a newspaper report that the government favoured a proposal for media ownership to be regulated by general competition laws instead of fixed share limits.
"That is an option and all of those options are being examined," he said when asked to comment on the report.
"We've had a lot of submissions from different people and in the end, you've got to achieve a sensible balance between local ownership and also diversity."
Under current cross-media regulations, media proprietors are not allowed to control both broadcast and print media in the same market.
